title: Playing with Chris Kelly and the Johnny Brown band
summary: Barnes talks about joining Kelly's band, its changing personnel, Johnny Brown's earlier band, and playing with Kelly before and after the Depression.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Well, after I got to Kelly, well I was probably stuck with Kelly, because he had lots of weight. And he was better than I was. I was getting plenty of weight myself, and I had a bar playing band, and we used to get lots of weight. Peter Patton, he would get plenty of weight too. Well, we had to, maybe if we'd get a job, we had to approach each other. Mm-hmm. I had to approach each other. Oh, you all used to get jobs, huh? Yeah. Who else was in that band then? Oh man, I couldn't call him, man. That band would change so much.

That band would change so much. Well, did Kelly have a band before you came into it? I mean, he had a band before he used you, he must use somebody else I'm crying at. Do you remember whose place you took in the band? No, I don't remember.
But he'd been playing for a while before you got with him. Before I went with him, yeah.
Did you ever know Johnny Brown?
Yeah, yeah, that's right. Johnny Brown worked with him. We used to work with Johnny Brown together. Oh, now wait a minute.
Johnny Brown had a band before Kelly?
Yeah. Johnny had a band before Kelly.
Well, who was playing trumpet with Johnny?
Well, I do remember who played trumpet with Johnny when Kelly didn't play. But most of his job was Kelly. He would use Kelly.
Oh, I see.
So it was Johnny Brown's band before. Yeah, yeah.
And then what happened to Johnny?
Well, I don't know. I think Johnny died. I think sure Johnny died. Because me, Johnny and Kelly, who were two together, Johnny was the player. All Johnny Brown.
Two parents, was that?
Yeah. But Johnny wasn't much of a country, you know.
Did he know many people or something?
Who? Johnny Brown. Johnny was well known. Yeah. Yeah, he was well first and more.
Oh, I see. And that's how he got contacts.
Yeah.
Hmm. So, well now, Kelly, did he die before Buddy Petita after?
Do you remember? Oh, no, no. No, long after.
Long after Buddy. Yeah. Long after. Did you play with Kelly before the pressure or after?

I played with Kelly before the pressure. Then after the pressure. There was lots of times that I carried my own band. That's how many men are scared of me today. They don't want to be bothering me. They scared me to take their way.
Yeah.
